body:
I need drafted dialogue for three short camp scenes with Kasimir Velikov. The party is a group of adventurers the player controls.

# Part B: three camp talks

When the party makes camp and rests for the night, Kasimir (travelling with the party as an ally) sometimes asks for a word by the fire: a short scene, played once. Each scene's shape: a node named for the scene: Narrator x1 (the fire and what he is doing, one or two sentences), then Kasimir x2 (his opening), then two party option rows (the player's character speaks, first person, short, under 14 words); then two reply nodes, named `<scene>_a` and `<scene>_b`, each Kasimir x2 or x1. The scene ends after the reply (do not write `-> END`).

1. castle_eve: the night before the party goes to Castle Ravenloft. Whatever happened to his sister, she is in or under that castle. He talks about the day they stoned her (the stones, the hands, the quiet after; he stood at the back) in one precise, unhurried image, and says what he would like to say to the count's face and knows he will not. Options: "You do not have to say anything to him." / "Then say it to us."
2. counting: he made the bargain at the temple (every year but one), and Patrina walked ahead of him. This is how he spends the nights now: counting what is left on the net's knots; what a year weighs now that he can count it; the strange freedom in it. No self-pity. Options: "Do you regret it?" / "What will you do with the year?"
3. peace: he made his peace with his sister's spirit at the temple (she was laid to rest, or he said what he owed her). A different night: he sleeps; the net lies unmended; he does not trust the quiet yet. Options: "Is it strange, being at peace?" / "What will you do after?"

Do not repeat his existing lines. About 22 lines.

## The game and the format

This is dialogue for a single-player D&D Curse of Strahd game. Plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables), nodes under `~ name`, one line per row as `Speaker [mood]: Text`, party option rows as `* option text -> node_name` (the player's character speaks, first person, short, under 14 words, no skill checks), ASCII only (straight quotes and apostrophes, no accents or fancy dashes, no em-dash: use a comma or a full stop), 1-2 sentences a line, nothing over about 28 words, no placeholders like {name}. Moods allowed: [smile], [angry], [afraid], [sad], [sly], [weary]; most lines carry none. Reply with the nodes below only, in the order given, no commentary. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## Who they are

KASIMIR VELIKOV: one of the last dusk elves in the valley, grave, soft-spoken, formal, with long patience and a self-mockery so dry it reads as sorrow; he never hurries. His people came to the valley as the vampire lord Strahd's guests and stayed as his tenants. His sister Patrina went up to the castle of her own will to learn what its lord knew; their own people stoned her for it, and Kasimir stood at the back with empty hands and did nothing, for three hundred years. He has lodged with the Vistani, mending a net he never casts. He believed a sealed temple of amber in the northern mountains could bring her back. Pet turns: "I am poor company. I have been poor company for a very long time." "The songs were written before the ending. They usually are." He never names Strahd ("the lord of the castle", "the count", "him").
Where the story stands for the nodes below (the node says which): either he made the bargain at the temple (he gave every year he had left but one and Patrina was restored, and she walked barefoot through the snow toward the castle and did not wait for him; he counts his last year), or Patrina was laid to rest at peace (and he made his peace).
Some of his existing lines, so you hear him (do NOT repeat them): "Patrina walked up these stairs of her own will. I stood at the back the day they stoned her for it. I am done standing at the back." / "Every morning I wake and count. The number is smaller. I would not take the bargain back. I would like to stop counting." / "She didn't wait. Of course she didn't wait. She never once waited for me." / "Then I will be brave once, and late. Take it." / "I think of her less as a wound now, and more as a name. It is a strange relief. I do not trust it yet." / "One year. It is strange, how much longer a year feels when you can count it." / "My people came over this pass as the count's guests. They are still his guests. It is the longest visit in the history of the world."
STRAHD: courteous, patient, amused host; never raises his voice; never threatens in these lines; a host's courtesy that is also a knife.
NARRATOR: old gothic storyteller, second person or plain scene description, present tense, one or two sentences, concrete senses, never cruel.

## Canon limits

No new named characters. Real names you may use: Kasimir, Patrina (his sister), Strahd only as a speaker label, Castle Ravenloft, the Amber Temple, Vallaki and the Vistani camp, Madam Eva. Do not name Strahd in a line. Do not invent other names, numbers, places or history. Do not show or describe Patrina alive on stage (she is "upstairs", "in the castle"). No quest hints, no directions, no promises. No dice or skill checks.
result:
~ castle_eve
Narrator: The campfire burns down to red ash in the dark below Castle Ravenloft. Kasimir sits with his empty hands open to the heat.
Kasimir: The day my people stoned Patrina, they wiped the gray dust from their palms afterward in complete silence. I stood at the back, and my hands were the only clean ones in the clearing.
Kasimir [weary]: I have rehearsed a speech for the count's face about the debt he owes our house. When the doors open tomorrow, I know I will not say a word of it.
* You do not have to say anything to him. -> castle_eve_a
* Then say it to us. -> castle_eve_b

~ castle_eve_a
Kasimir: No, words are only another way to stand at the back and wait. He has listened to men speak for centuries, and it has never once spoiled his evening.
Kasimir: Better to bring cold iron into his house than another speech.

~ castle_eve_b
Kasimir [sad]: I would tell him that he took a scholar who wanted his books and left us a grave we had to dig ourselves. Look how small it sounds in the open air.
Kasimir: I am glad I spent it by your fire instead of at his table.

~ counting
Narrator: Firelight catches the hemp cord draped across Kasimir's knees. He moves his thumb from knot to knot, unhurried and precise.
Kasimir: At the Amber Temple I traded away the rest of my life for Patrina's breath, and she walked ahead into the snow without looking back. Now I tie a knot in this old net for each night that remains of my last year.
Kasimir: A year has an astonishing weight when you can hold the whole of it in two hands. There is a strange freedom in knowing the exact measure of the rope.
* Do you regret it? -> counting_a
* What will you do with the year? -> counting_b

~ counting_a
Kasimir: Regret is a luxury for men who still have centuries to waste by a Vistani wagon. My sister is out of the dark, and the price was only the time I had failed to use.
Kasimir [smile]: I am a poor merchant, perhaps, but I am satisfied with the trade.

~ counting_b
Kasimir: Walk with you into Castle Ravenloft, first, and see what my sister has made of her second life. After that, I may cast this net into a real river just to see if it holds water.

~ peace
Narrator: The old net lies folded and unmended beside Kasimir's pack as the embers settle. He sits with his cloak drawn up, watching the sparks rise into the pines.
Kasimir: For the first time since the stones fell on Patrina, I slept through the night without waking to her voice. We said what was owed at the Amber Temple, and she is finally still.
Kasimir [weary]: The silence in my head is very wide, and I do not quite trust the quiet yet. A man who carries a stone for an age walks crookedly when he sets it down.
* Is it strange, being at peace? -> peace_a
* What will you do after? -> peace_b

~ peace_a
Kasimir: It feels like stepping out of the Vistani tents into snow that has fallen all night. Everything is clean, and none of the old landmarks are where I left them.

~ peace_b
Kasimir: Finish our business with the lord of the castle, if the morning lets us. Then I think I will leave this net by the water and learn what my hands are for when they are not mending.
Kasimir [smile]: I am a little late to begin a life, I know, but I have never been a hurried man.
